title: Design System: Ithaca for Plex App Store one-sheets

display.purpose: The slide's two-line claim, each line fitted to the title width, closing punctuation hung.

headline.purpose: The product page header's title, inside the crop-safe area.

label.purpose: Billing lines, each fitted edge to edge to the billing width.

label-role.purpose: Half-size credit words inside billing lines (PICTURE IN, SOUND IN, ALSO STARRING).

title.purpose: One short tracked line at top centre.

body.purpose: One tracked sentence at the bottom, shrunk to 90% of the slide width when long.

shadows.name: device-rim
shadows.purpose: The drawn bezel edge of every device.

shadows.name: device-drop
shadows.purpose: Soft fall-off below the device onto the shelf.

components.name: Title
components.description: Two-line Anton claim, lines fitted to one width, closing punctuation hung outside it.
components.css: .ds-title { margin: 0; padding: 24px; background: #0B0B0D; color: #fff; font-family: Anton, Impact, sans-serif; font-weight: 400; text-transform: uppercase; text-align: center; font-size: 64px; } .ds-title span { display: block; line-height: .867em; } .ds-title span + span { margin-top: .14em; } .ds-title em { font-style: normal; margin-right: -.236em; }

components.name: Billing Block
components.description: Credit lines in Six Caps, fitted edge to edge, with half-size raised role labels.
components.html: PICTURE IN 4K · HEVC · DOLBY VISION 7 AND 8 · HDR10+ · HLGSOUND IN DOLBY ATMOS · DTS-HD MA · FLAC · AC-3 · AAC
components.css: .ds-bill { margin: 0; padding: 20px; background: #0B0B0D; color: rgba(255,255,255,.84); font: 32px/1 'Six Caps', 'Bebas Neue', sans-serif; letter-spacing: .05em; text-align: center; } .ds-bill span { display: block; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.02; } .ds-bill i { font-style: normal; font-size: .5em; letter-spacing: .12em; vertical-align: .32em; margin: 0 .3em; }

components.name: Tagline
components.description: One short tracked line at top centre of the poster.
components.css: .ds-tag { margin: 0; padding: 16px; background: #0B0B0D; color: #fff; text-align: center; font: 28px/1 'Six Caps', sans-serif; letter-spacing: .34em; padding-left: calc(16px + .34em); text-transform: uppercase; }

components.name: Foot Line
components.description: One tracked Anton sentence at the bottom, where a one-sheet puts its release line.
components.html: Your progress catches up when you land.
components.css: .ds-foot { margin: 0; padding: 16px; background: #0B0B0D; color: #fff; text-align: center; white-space: nowrap; font: 14px/1 Anton, Impact, sans-serif; letter-spacing: .24em; text-transform: uppercase; }

components.name: Resume Line
components.description: 6px progress bar under the device, filled in white to the slide's stop fraction.
components.css: .ds-stage { padding: 24px; background: #0B0B0D; } .ds-stop { position: relative; width: 100%; height: 6px; border-radius: 3px; background: rgba(255,255,255,.16); } .ds-stop:before { content: ''; position: absolute; inset: 0 auto 0 0; width: var(--stop); border-radius: 3px; background: #fff; }

components.name: Device Frame
components.description: The drawn device: device-black body, padding equal to the frame width, rim and soft drop. The screen inside is a real capture.
components.css: .ds-stage { padding: 32px; background: #0B0B0D; display: flex; justify-content: center; } .ds-dev { padding: 6px; border-radius: 37px; background: #050506; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px #33363E, inset 0 0 0 2px rgba(255,255,255,.06), 0 18px 35px rgba(0,0,0,.65); } .ds-screen { width: 120px; height: 261px; border-radius: 31px; background: linear-gradient(#2E5E6E, #0B0B0D); }

narrative.overview:
Every slide is a theatrical one-sheet poster. The device is the key art, the claim is the title, and a billing block credits what Ithaca plays the way a film poster credits its cast. The film on the device's screen continues past the frame as the poster's art, darkened and pulled toward poster black, so the slide reads as one picture with a device standing in it rather than a phone floating on a gradient.

The world is black, white and the film's own colour. There is no brand colour, no gradient for its own sake, no badge, card or logo. Type is condensed and poster-like: Anton for the claim and the foot line, Six Caps for the tagline and billing. The only lit marks are the screen and a thin resume line under the device.

The set is read as a row in the App Store, so all slides of a device class share one central axis and one shelf line. The product page header carries the same world without a device: a letterboxed 4K film frame with the title in Apple's crop-safe area.

This covers only the App Store marketing surface. STYLE.md governs the app's own UI.
keyCharacteristics: Poster black canvas; white type only.
The device is drawn (frame and rim are the build's own), centred, standing on a fixed shelf line.
Key art is the actual picture the app shows on that screen, continuing past the frame.
Two-line uppercase Anton title, each line fitted to the same width, final punctuation hung.
Billing block in Six Caps, every line fitted edge to edge, with half-size role labels.
A resume line under the device as the single progress mark.

rules.name: The Film's Own Colour Rule
rules.body: The only hue on a slide is the hue of the film on its screen. Ithaca's brand accent never appears on the marketing surface; per STYLE.md it lives in the icon only.

rules.name: The Darkened Art Rule
rules.body: Key art always sits below the type in value: brightness .52 and saturation .75 for the sharp layer, brightness .45 and a 14px blur for the soft layer (brightness .42 on the header), then the film tint.

rules.name: The Hung Punctuation Rule
rules.body: A title's closing period or question mark sits outside the fitted width (margin-right: -.236em), so the letters, not the punctuation, align to the measure. A mid-line mark on the one-line Apple TV title is not hung.

rules.name: The Fitted Billing Rule
rules.body: Billing lines are set edge to edge like a poster's credit block: each line scaled to the block width, never left ragged, never wrapped.

rules.name: The Credit Wording Rule
rules.body: Billing reads as credits: role label in small caps, then the claims in full caps, separated by middots. Claims are real features only; no invented reviews, awards or numbers.

rules.name: The Shelf Rule
rules.body: One central axis and one shelf line per device class. A slide never moves the device to make room for copy; copy fits to the slide.

rules.name: The Continuing Art Rule
rules.body: Where the screen shows a hero picture, the same art is placed sharp at the exact position the app draws it (place, measured with place.py), so it continues past the frame. It fades out at its own edges (6% sides, 7% top, from 80% down) into a blurred copy of itself, and the whole art layer fades to poster black between the fade stops. Screens with no hero, and Apple TV, get only the soft layer.

rules.name: The Drawn Frame Rule
rules.body: The device frame is drawn by the build. Nothing is placed over Apple's device bezels or mockups; Apple's terms allow nothing over their bezels, so the build owns the frame.

dos: Do use as key art only the picture the app shows on that captured screen, from Blender Studio open movies or public-domain films, with its source and licence listed in docs/app-store/keyart/SOURCES.txt.
Do keep one central axis and one shelf line per device class.
Do fit every billing line edge to edge and every title line to the same width.
Do tint the art toward black with the film's own colour.
Do draw the device frame in the build.
Do embed provenance in every shipped raster (impeccable embed-prompt), naming the capture and key art it was composed from.
Do scale the 6.3" iPhone set from the 6.9" renders rather than laying it out separately.
donts: Don't use logos (Plex, Dolby, DTS, Apple or any other), third-party studio art, or any celebrity likeness.
Don't capture with any account other than the demo account; other libraries show other studios' posters.
Don't put anything over Apple's bezels; the frame is drawn.
Don't add decorative gradients, badges, cards, ratings or invented reviews and awards.
Don't use the brand accent or any colour that is not the film's own.
Don't move a device off the shared shelf or axis to make room for copy.
Don't apply anything in this file to the app's UI; STYLE.md governs the app.
